question: In March 2026, the Finnish Border Guard carried out a four-day training exercise at three closed border crossings with Russia – an exercise in which the European Gendarmerie Force (EUROGENDFOR) was involved for the first time. The aim was to test a new border protection law that empowers authorities to push back asylum seekers and use force under certain conditions.
Frontex also participated and, according to its own statements, undertook tasks such as mobile surveillance, weapons and document checks, and the securing of transports. 1.
How does the Council assess the compatibility of this with the fundamental right to asylum and the principle of non-refoulement?
Which Member States and other actors were involved in the exercise, and in what proportions were Frontex, EUROGENDFOR and Finnish and Estonian officials involved?
answer: The Council has not discussed this question.
